" الْغُبَيْرَاءِ "
 وَكَانَ قَوْلُهُمْ وَاعْتِقَادُهُمْ فِيهَا أَنَّهَا مَعْصِيَةٌ وَسَيِّئَةٌ؛ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُمْ مَعَ ذَلِكَ يَقُولُونَ فِي اعْتِقَادِهِمْ بِدَلِيلِ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى وَهُوَ 
{إنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ}
 وَذَكَرُوا أَيْضًا أَنَّهَا حَرَامٌ؛ غَيْرَ أَنَّ لَهُمْ وِرْدًا بِاللَّيْلِ وَتَعَبُّدَاتٍ وَيَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهَا إذَا حَصَلَتْ نَشْوَتُهَا بِرُءُوسِهِمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ بِتِلْكَ الْعِبَادَةِ وَلَا تَأْمُرُهُمْ بِسُوءِ وَلَا فَاحِشَةٍ وَنَسَبُوا أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهَا ضَرَرٌ لِأَحَدِ مِنْ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى كَالزِّنَا وَشُرْبِ الْخَمْرِ وَالسَّرِقَةِ وَأَنَّهُ لَا يَجِبُ عَلَى مَنْ أَكَلَهَا حَدٌّ مِنْ الْحُدُودِ؛ إلَّا أَنَّهَا تَتَعَلَّقُ بِمُخَالَفَةِ أَمْرٍ مِنْ أُمُورِ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى وَاَللَّهُ يَغْفِرُ مَا بَيْنَ الْعَبْدِ وَرَبِّهِ.
 وَاجْتَمَعَ بِهِمْ رَجُلٌ صَادِقُ الْقَوْلِ وَذَكَرَ عَنْهُمْ ذَلِكَ وَوَافَقَهُمْ عَلَى أَكْلِهَا بِحُكْمِهِمْ عَلَيْهِ وَحَدِيثِهِمْ لَهُ وَاعْتَرَفَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بِذَلِكَ:
 فَهَلْ يَجِبُ عَلَى آكِلِهَا حَدُّ شَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ أَمْ لَا؟ أَفْتُونَا.
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

“There is a group of Muslim men, middle-aged and young, who have performed Hajj and diligently fulfil their obligations of fasting, prayer, and worship. Among them are men of high standing, and they are known among Muslims for their trustworthiness and honesty in word and deed. They show no outward signs of evil or wickedness. Yet they are of one mind and opinion about eating ‘al-ghubayrāʾ’. They acknowledge and believe that doing so is an act of disobedience and a sin. Nevertheless, they cite in support of their view the words in the Book of Allah—glorified and exalted is He:

‘Indeed, good deeds wipe out evil deeds.’

“They also acknowledge that it is forbidden. However, they have regular nightly devotions and other acts of worship, and they claim that when its intoxication takes hold of their minds, it prompts them to perform those acts of worship, not to commit evil or indecency. They maintain that it does not harm any of Allah Most High’s creatures in the way that unlawful sexual intercourse, drinking wine, and theft do, and that whoever consumes it is not liable to any prescribed punishment. Rather, it merely involves contravening one of the commands of Allah—glorified and exalted is He—and Allah forgives matters that are between a servant and his Lord.

“A truthful man met with them and reported these things about them. He joined them in consuming it, relying on the judgment they gave him and what they told him, and admitted to having done so.

“Is someone who consumes it liable to the prescribed punishment for drinking wine, or not? Please give us a ruling.”

original_text:
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، نَعَمْ يَجِبُ عَلَى آكِلِهَا حَدُّ شَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ.
 وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْقَوْمُ ضُلَّالٌ جُهَّالٌ عُصَاةٌ لِلَّهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَكَفَى بِرَجُلِ جَهْلًا أَنْ يَعْرِفَ بِأَنَّ هَذَا الْفِعْلَ مُحَرَّمٌ وَأَنَّهُ مَعْصِيَةٌ لِلَّهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ:
 إنَّهُ تَطِيبُ لَهُ الْعِبَادَةُ وَتَصْلُحُ لَهُ حَالُهُ وَيْحُ هَذَا الْقَائِلِ أَيَظُنُّ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى وَرَسُولَهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَرَّمَ عَلَى الْخَلْقِ مَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَيُصْلِحُ لَهُمْ حَالَهُمْ نَعَمْ قَدْ يَكُونُ فِي الشَّيْءِ مَنْفَعَةٌ وَفِيهِ مَضَرَّةٌ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ مَنْفَعَتِهِ فَيُحَرِّمُهُ اللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى؛
 لِأَنَّ الْمَضَرَّةَ إذَا كَانَتْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ الْمَنْفَعَةِ بَقِيَتْ الزِّيَادَةُ مَضَرَّةً مَحْضَةً وَصَارَ هَذَا الرَّجُلُ كَأَنَّهُ قَالَ لِرَجُلِ:
 خُذْ مِنِّي هَذَا الدِّرْهَمَ وَاعْطِنِي دِينَارًا فَجَهْلُهُ يَقُولُ لَهُ: هُوَ يُعْطِيك دِرْهَمًا فَخُذْهُ وَالْعَقْلُ يَقُولُ: إنَّمَا يَحْصُلُ الدِّرْهَمُ بِفَوَاتِ الدِّينَارِ وَهَذَا ضَرَرٌ لَا مَنْفَعَةَ لَهُ؛ بَلْ جَمِيعُ مَا حَرَّمَهُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ إنْ ثَبَتَ فِيهِ مَنْفَعَةٌ مَا فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ ضَرَرُهُ أَكْثَرَ. فَهَذِهِ 
" الْحَشِيشَةُ الْمَلْعُونَةُ "
 هِيَ وَآكِلُوهَا وَمُسْتَحِلُّوهَا الْمُوجِبَةُ لِسُخْطِ اللَّهِ وَسُخْطِ رَسُولِهِ وَسُخْطِ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الْمُعَرِّضَةُ صَاحِبَهَا لِعُقُوبَةِ اللَّهِ؛
 إذَا كَانَتْ كَمَا يَقُولُهُ الضَّالُّونَ:
 مِنْ أَنَّهَا تَجْمَعُ الْهِمَّةَ: وَتَدْعُو إلَى الْعِبَادَةِ فَإِنَّهَا مُشْتَمِلَةٌ عَلَى ضَرَرٍ فِي دِينِ الْمَرْءِ وَعَقْلِهِ وَخُلُقِهِ وَطَبْعِهِ أَضْعَافَ مَا فِيهَا مِنْ خَيْرٍ؛ وَلَا خَيْرَ فِيهَا؛ وَلَكِنْ هِيَ تُحَلِّلُ الرُّطُوبَاتِ؛ فَتَتَصَاعَدُ الْأَبْخِرَةُ إلَى الدِّمَاغِ؛ وَتُورِثُ خَيَالَاتٍ فَاسِدَةً فَيَهُونُ عَلَى الْمَرْءِ مَا يَفْعَلُهُ مِنْ عِبَادَةٍ؛ وَيَشْغَلُهُ بِتِلْكَ التَّخَيُّلَاتِ عَنْ إضْرَارِ النَّاسِ. وَهَذِهِ رِشْوَةُ الشَّيْطَانِ يَرْشُو بِهَا الْمُبْطِلِينَ لِيُطِيعُوهُ
translated_text:
He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. Yes, whoever consumes it is liable to the prescribed punishment for drinking wine.

These people are misguided, ignorant, and disobedient to Allah and His Messenger. It is ignorance enough for a man to know that an act is forbidden and constitutes disobedience to Allah and His Messenger, yet say that it makes worship enjoyable for him and improves his condition. Woe to whoever says this! Does he imagine that Allah—glorified and exalted is He—and His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—have forbidden people what benefits them and improves their condition?

Certainly, something may contain some benefit but cause greater harm, so Allah—glorified and exalted is He—forbids it. When the harm outweighs the benefit, the excess remains pure harm. Such a man is like someone who says to another, “Take this dirham from me and give me a dinar.” His ignorance tells him, “He is giving you a dirham, so take it,” while reason says, “You obtain the dirham only by losing the dinar.” This is harm without benefit. Indeed, whatever Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, if it is established that it contains any benefit at all, its harm must necessarily be greater.

As for this “accursed hashish”—accursed along with those who consume it and those who deem it lawful—which incurs the displeasure of Allah, His Messenger, and His believing servants, and exposes its user to Allah’s punishment: if it does, as the misguided claim, concentrate one’s resolve and prompt one to worship, then the harm it causes to a person’s religion, reason, character, and disposition is many times greater than whatever good it contains. Yet there is no good in it. Rather, it dissolves bodily moisture, causing vapours to rise to the brain and producing corrupt imaginings. This makes whatever worship a person performs seem easy to him, while those imaginings distract him from harming people. This is Satan’s bribe, with which he bribes the followers of falsehood so that they will obey him

original_text:
فِيهَا؛ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْفِضَّةِ الْقَلِيلَةِ فِي الدِّرْهَمِ الْمَغْشُوشِ؛ وَكُلُّ مَنْفَعَةٍ تَحْصُلُ بِهَذَا السَّبَبِ فَإِنَّهَا تَنْقَلِبُ مَضَرَّةً فِي الْمَآلِ؛ وَلَا يُبَارَكُ لِصَاحِبِهَا فِيهَا؛ وَإِنَّمَا هَذَا نَظِيرَ السَّكْرَانِ بِالْخَمْرِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا تَطِيشُ عَقْلَهُ حَتَّى يَسْخُوَ بِمَالِهِ؛ وَيَتَشَجَّعَ عَلَى أَقْرَانِهِ؛ فَيَعْتَقِدُ الْغِرُّ أَنَّهَا أَوْرَثَتْهُ السَّخَاءَ وَالشَّجَاعَةَ وَهُوَ جَاهِلٌ؛ وَإِنَّمَا أَوْرَثَتْهُ عَدَمَ الْعَقْلِ. وَمَنْ لَا عَقْلَ لَهُ لَا يَعْرِفُ قَدْرَ النَّفْسِ وَالْمَالِ فَيَجُودُ بِجَهْلِهِ؛ لَا عَنْ عَقْلٍ فِيهِ. وَكَذَلِكَ هَذِهِ الْحَشِيشَةُ الْمُسْكِرَةُ إذَا أَضْعَفَتْ الْعَقْلَ؛
 وَفَتَحَتْ بَابَ الْخَيَالِ:
 تَبْقَى الْعَادَةُ فِيهَا مِثْلَ الْعِبَادَاتِ فِي الدِّينِ الْبَاطِلِ دِينِ النَّصَارَى؛ فَإِنَّ الرَّاهِبَ تَجِدُهُ يَجْتَهِدُ فِي أَنْوَاعِ الْعِبَادَةِ لَا يَفْعَلُهَا الْمُسْلِمُ الْحَنِيفُ؛ فَإِنَّ دِينَهُ بَاطِلٌ وَالْبَاطِلُ خَفِيفٌ وَلِهَذَا تَجُودُ النُّفُوسُ فِي السَّمَاعِ الْمُحَرَّمِ وَالْعِشْرَةِ الْمُحَرَّمَةِ بِالْأَمْوَالِ وَحُسْنِ الْخُلُقِ بِمَا لَا تَجُودُ بِهِ فِي الْحَقِّ؛ وَمَا هَذَا بِاَلَّذِي يُبِيحُ تِلْكَ الْمَحَارِمِ أَوْ يَدْعُو الْمُؤْمِنُ إلَى فِعْلِهِ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ إنَّمَا كَانَ لِأَنَّ الطَّبْعَ لَمَّا أَخَذَ نَصِيبَهُ مِنْ الْحَظِّ الْمُحَرَّمِ وَلَمْ يُبَالِ بِمَا بَذَلَهُ عِوَضًا عَنْ ذَلِكَ؛ وَلَيْسَ فِي هَذَا مَنْفَعَةٌ فِي دِينِ الْمَرْءِ وَلَا دُنْيَاهُ؛ وَإِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ لَذَّةُ سَاعَةٍ بِمَنْزِلَةِ لَذَّةِ الزَّانِي حَالَ الْفِعْلِ وَلَذَّةُ شِفَاءِ الْغَضَبِ حَالَ الْقَتْلِ وَلَذَّةُ الْخَمْرِ حَالَ النَّشْوَةِ ثُمَّ إذَا صَحَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَجَدَ عَمَلَهُ بَاطِلًا وَذُنُوبَهُ مُحِيطَةً بِهِ وَقَدْ نَقَصَ عَلَيْهِ عَقْلُهُ وَدِينُهُ وَخُلُقُهُ. وَأَيْنَ هَؤُلَاءِ الضُّلَّالُ مِمَّا تُورِثُهُ هَذِهِ الْمَلْعُونَةُ مِنْ قِلَّةِ الْغَيْرَةِ؛ وَزَوَالِ الْحَمِيَّةِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ آكِلُهَا إمَّا دَيُّوثًا وَإِمَّا مَأْبُونًا؛ وَإِمَّا كِلَاهُمَا. وَتُفْسِدُ الْأَمْزِجَةَ
translated_text:
in this; it is like the small amount of silver in an adulterated dirham. Every benefit obtained by such means ultimately turns into harm, and brings its recipient no blessing. This is just like someone intoxicated by wine: it unsettles his reason until he spends his wealth freely and boldly confronts his peers. The naive imagine that it has endowed him with generosity and courage, but they are ignorant: it has merely deprived him of reason. Someone without reason does not appreciate the value of life or wealth, so he gives generously out of ignorance, not sound judgment.

Likewise, when this intoxicating hashish weakens reason and opens the door to fantasy, habitual practice under its influence resembles acts of worship in the false religion of Christianity. You find a monk exerting himself in forms of worship that a Muslim devoted to pure monotheism would not undertake. His religion is false, and falsehood is easy to bear. Similarly, in unlawful listening sessions and unlawful companionship, people display a generosity with their wealth and a pleasantness of character that they do not display in pursuing the truth. Yet this neither makes those forbidden things lawful nor invites a believer to engage in them. It happens only because, once a person’s natural inclinations have received their share of forbidden pleasure, he no longer cares what he gives in exchange.

There is no benefit in this for a person’s religious or worldly life. It is merely a moment’s pleasure, like the pleasure of someone committing unlawful intercourse during the act, the pleasure of venting anger while killing, or the pleasure of wine during intoxication. Then, when he comes to his senses, he finds his deeds worthless and his sins surrounding him, while his reason, religion, and character have all deteriorated.

Do these misguided people not consider how this accursed substance diminishes protective jealousy and destroys the sense of honour, until its consumer becomes either a man who tolerates sexual immorality in his family, a man who submits to sodomy, or both? It also corrupts bodily temperaments

original_text:
حَتَّى جَعَلَتْ خَلْقًا كَثِيرًا مَجَانِينَ وَتَجْعَلُ الْكَبِدَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ السفتج وَمَنْ لَمْ يُجَنَّ مِنْهُمْ فَقَدْ أَعْطَتْهُ نَقْصَ الْعَقْلِ وَلَوْ صَحَا مِنْهَا فَإِنَّهُ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي عَقْلِهِ خَبَلٌ؛ ثُمَّ إنَّ كَثِيرَهَا يُسْكِرُ حَتَّى يَصُدَّ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنْ الصَّلَاةِ وَهِيَ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَا تُوجِبُ قُوَّةَ نَفْسِ صَاحِبِهَا حَتَّى يُضَارِبَ وَيُشَاتِمَ فَكَفَى بِالرَّجُلِ شَرًّا أَنَّهَا تَصُدُّهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنْ الصَّلَاةِ إذَا سَكِرَ مِنْهَا وَقَلِيلُهَا وَإِنْ لَمْ يُسْكِرْ فَهُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ قَلِيلِ الْخَمْرِ.
 ثُمَّ إنَّهَا تُورِثُ مِنْ مَهَانَةِ آكِلِهَا وَدَنَاءَةِ نَفْسِهِ وَانْفِتَاحِ شَهْوَتِهِ:

{كُلُّ مُسْكِرٍ خَمْرٌ؛ وَكُلُّ مُسْكِرٍ حَرَامٌ}

translated_text:
to the point that it has driven many people insane, and it makes the liver like suftaj. Those whom it has not driven insane have nevertheless suffered diminished reason. Even after they sober up, some impairment of their reason inevitably remains. Moreover, large quantities cause intoxication that turns a person away from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. Although it does not embolden its consumer to fight and exchange insults, it is evil enough that, when he becomes intoxicated by it, it turns him away from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. A small quantity, even if it does not intoxicate, is like a small quantity of wine.

Furthermore, it brings upon its consumer a degree of humiliation, baseness of character, and unrestrained desire that wine does not. It thus has harmful effects absent from wine, although wine has a harmful effect absent from it: belligerence. Hashish therefore deserves prohibition even more than wine, because the harm its consumer inflicts upon himself is greater than that caused by wine, whereas the wine drinker’s harm to others is greater. In these times, however, the widespread consumption of hashish has made its harm to others greater than that of wine.

Allah has forbidden prohibited things because they harm those who engage in them. Were they to harm others without harming the person engaging in them, He would not have forbidden them. An envious person, for example, is harmed by the good fortune of the person he envies, yet Allah has not forbidden the attainment of distinction merely to spare the envious person that harm.

Moreover, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden.”

Hashish is intoxicating. Even if no wording specifically encompassed it, it would still contain the harmful effects for which wine was forbidden, besides other harmful effects not found in wine that require its prohibition. And Allah knows best.

Chapter on Discretionary Punishment

Shaykh al-Islām Abū al-‘Abbās was asked:

A Muslim emir owns slaves and has attendants in his service. May he carry out a prescribed punishment on any of them who commits an offense warranting it? May he command them to fulfill an obligation they neglect, such as the five daily prayers and similar duties? What kind of whip should he use to punish them?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. He must command them all to do what is right and forbid them from wrongdoing and aggression. At the very least, whenever he hires one of them, he must stipulate this as a condition, just as he stipulates the work to be performed. Whenever any of them fails to comply, he should dismiss him.

If he is able to punish them, with the ruler allowing him to do so under prevailing custom, while no one else punishes them because they are under his protection or for a similar reason, then he should administer discretionary punishment if they will neither fulfill their obligations nor refrain from prohibited acts without punishment. In that case, he is the one charged with this duty, for he is able to carry it out, whereas others

He was also asked—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

Concerning a senior military commander known for goodness and religious devotion: one of the collectors of unlawful levies made false accusations against him, going so far as to beat him, suspend him, parade him on a donkey, and then imprison him. Must the ruler have the man who wronged him beaten?

He replied:

The person who falsely accused him and wronged him in this manner must, by agreement of the Muslims, receive a punishment that deters him and others like him from such conduct. Indeed, the majority of the early generations affirm retaliation in kind in such cases: whoever unjustly beats and wounds another is to be treated as he treated his victim.

As ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb said:

“O people, I did not send my officials to you to beat you or take your wealth, but to teach you the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of your Prophet, and to distribute your public revenues among you. Whenever I learn that someone has been beaten unjustly by his official, I will grant him retaliation.”

ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀs challenged him on this, whereupon he said to them:

“The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) exacted retaliation from those who wronged him.”

فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْهِ بِالشَّتْمِ وَالسَّبِّ فَلَهُ أَنْ يَعْتَدِيَ عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَى عَلَيْهِ؛
 فَيَشْتُمَهُ إذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ مُحَرَّمًا لِعَيْنِهِ:
 كَالْكَذِبِ. وَأَمَّا إنْ كَانَ مُحَرَّمًا لِعَيْنِهِ كَالْقَذْفِ بِغَيْرِ الزِّنَا فَإِنَّهُ يُعَزَّرُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ تَعْزِيرًا بَلِيغًا يَرْدَعُهُ وَأَمْثَالَهُ مِنْ السُّفَهَاءِ وَلَوْ عُزِّرَ عَلَى النَّوْعِ الْأَوَّلِ مِنْ الشَّتْمِ جَازَ؛ وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَشْرَعُ إذَا تَكَرَّرَ سَفَهُهُ أَوْ عُدْوَانُهُ عَلَى مَنْ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ مِنْهُ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
عَمَّنْ شَتَمَ رَجُلًا فَقَالَ لَهُ:
 أَنْتَ مَلْعُونٌ وَلَدُ زِنًا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
يَجِبُ تَعْزِيرُهُ عَلَى هَذَا الْكَلَامِ وَيَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ حَدُّ الْقَذْفِ إنْ لَمْ يَقْصِدْ بِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ مَا يَقْصِدُهُ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ النَّاسِ مِنْ قَصْدِهِمْ بِهَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةِ أَنَّ الْمَشْتُومَ فِعْلُهُ خَبِيثٌ كَفِعْلِ وَلَدِ الزِّنَا.
translated_text:
He was also asked—may Allah sanctify his soul:

What is the ruling on someone who insults and reviles another man?

He replied:

If someone wrongs him by insulting and reviling him, he may respond in kind, insulting him in return, provided that his response is not intrinsically forbidden, as lying is. If, however, the insult is intrinsically forbidden, such as slander not involving an accusation of unlawful sexual intercourse, the offender is to receive a severe discretionary punishment that deters him and other foolish people like him. Discretionary punishment is also permissible for the first kind of insult; indeed, this is the prescribed course when his insolence or aggression against someone better than himself is repeated. And Allah knows best.

He was also asked—may Allah Most High have mercy on him:

What is the ruling on someone who insults another man, saying, “You are accursed, a child born of unlawful intercourse”?

He replied:

He must receive a discretionary punishment for these words. He must also receive the prescribed punishment for an accusation of unlawful sexual intercourse if, by this expression, he did not intend what many people intend by it: that the conduct of the person insulted is vile, like that of a child born of unlawful intercourse.

translated_text:
He replied:

If the person who was beaten is under his father’s guardianship, neither his settlement nor his release of the other party from liability is valid. Whatever his father paid because of this false accusation, he may recover from whoever wrongfully made him pay it, whether or not the son released that person from liability. The person who was beaten is entitled to inflict an equivalent beating on any of his accusers who called for him to be beaten, provided that he had not previously been known for wrongdoing.

Al-Nu‘mān ibn Bashīr stated that this was the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, as reported by {Abū Dāwūd and others. When some people asked him to beat a man on suspicion, he said: “If you wish, I will beat him for you; but if your property is not found in his possession, I will beat you just as I beat him.” They asked: “Is this your ruling?” He replied: “This is the ruling of Allah and His Messenger.”}

This concerns beating someone who was not known for wrongdoing. Beating someone known for wrongdoing is a different matter. Retaliation in kind for beating, slapping, and similar acts is established in reports from the Rightly Guided Caliphs and other Companions and Successors. It is also established in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and was expressly affirmed by several leading scholars, including Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Although many jurists do not recognize retaliation in kind in such cases, holding instead that discretionary punishment applies, the former view is correct.

But may the father exact the retaliation to which his son is entitled, or must he leave it until the son reaches adulthood? There is a well-known disagreement among scholars concerning this. If the son is already an adult, however, he himself has the right to exact corporal punishment and to retain that right.

Chapter: Amputation for Theft

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man’s house was repeatedly burgled. Later, after he had locked its door, a slave was found inside. He was apprehended and admitted that he had entered the house stealthily on numerous occasions, but did not admit to taking anything. Is he liable for what they have lost from the house? What is the ruling concerning him?

He replied:

This slave is to be punished, by the consensus of the Muslims, for his proven entry into the house. Many scholars also hold that he is to be punished.

If he makes an admission establishing that he took the property—for example, by indicating where it is, or to whom he gave it, or something similar—the property is to be recovered and returned to its owner if it still exists. If it has been lost or destroyed, he must compensate for it.

The person administering his punishment should use ingenuity to induce him to confess, as skilled judges and governors do with those whose wrongdoing becomes apparent to them, until he admits it. At the very least, the referral of the oath to the claimant should be attested against them. If the owner of the property then swears the oath, judgment is given in his favor upon his oath.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man owns a slave whom he alleges stole some of his belongings. The slave states that he deposited them with his former master, wrapped in a kerchief. Is his statement concerning this to be accepted? What must be done in this matter?

He replied:

By the consensus of the Muslims, no action may be taken solely on the slave’s statement, whether the official adjudicating between them is a military governor or a judge. Rather, the majority of jurists hold that, when someone is suspected of theft or a similar offence, his character must be examined. He may be known for wrongdoing, or his character may be unknown. If he is known for righteousness, it is not permissible to proceed against him or punish him. Scholars hold two views on whether he must swear an oath. Some also hold that whoever levels the accusation against him should receive a discretionary punishment.

If his character is unknown, he is to be detained until his circumstances are investigated. One view is that he should be detained for a month; another is that the duration is left to the ruler’s judgment. This is based on the report in the Sunan collections, narrated by Bahz ibn Hakīm, from his father, from his grandfather:

“The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, detained someone on suspicion.”

He replied:

As for allegations of theft, highway robbery and similar offenses, he may not entrust their investigation to someone whom he considers likely to act unjustly when he can appoint upright people to handle them to the extent possible. This is because people under suspicion fall into three categories.

One category consists of those known among the people for religious commitment and piety, who are not the sort to attract suspicion. Such a person is neither detained nor beaten. Indeed, according to one of the two scholarly opinions, he is not even required to swear an oath. Rather, many scholars state that whoever accuses him should be disciplined.

The second category consists of those whose character is unknown: they are known neither for righteousness nor for wickedness. Such a person is detained until his character has been investigated. Some have said that he is detained for a month; others have said that the length of detention is determined by the authority’s judgment. The basis for this is the report narrated by Abū Dāwūd and others:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, detained a man on suspicion.”

The imams have expressly affirmed this. Such a case is comparable to that of a person against whom someone brings a claim: he must attend the hearing before the authority adjudicating between them, even though this keeps him from his affairs. Likewise, this suspect may be kept from his affairs until his situation becomes known. Then, if inquiries reveal him to be righteous, he is released. If he is found to be wicked, he belongs to the third category: a wicked person who is known to have committed theft before, or is known for things that lead to theft—for example, someone who is

known for gambling and immoral practices that require money, although he has none, and the like. Such circumstances strengthen the suspicion against him. For this reason, a group of scholars have said that such a person may be interrogated by beating: the governor or judge may beat him—as stated by Ashhab, Mālik’s associate, and others—until he admits taking the property.

Another group have said that the governor may beat him, but not the judge. This was the position of a group of al-Shāfiʿī’s and Ahmad’s followers, as mentioned by the two judges, al-Māwardī and Abū Yaʿlā, in their respective works entitled al-Ahkām al-Sultāniyya (The Ordinances of Governance). It is also the position of a group of Mālikī scholars, as mentioned by al-Tarsūsī and others.

The official in charge may intend, through beating him, both to elicit a confession and to punish him for his known wickedness. Thus, the beating serves both as a disciplinary punishment and as a means of eliciting a confession. The official is not required to release all suspects until the owners of the property produce evidence identifying the thief.

“Rather, Allah revealed to His Prophet, concerning a case involving suspicion of theft, His words, Most High:

‘Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.’

‘And seek Allah’s forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.’

‘And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love anyone who is treacherous and sinful.’

‘They conceal themselves from people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah. He is with them when they plot by night words that displease Him. And Allah fully encompasses all that they do.’

‘Here you are, arguing on their behalf in this worldly life—but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their defender?’

 فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ " وَلَمْ يَقُلْ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِصَاحِبِ الْمَالِ: أَقِمْ الْبَيِّنَةَ؛ وَلَا حَلِّفْ الْمُتَّهَمِينَ؛ لِأَنَّ أُولَئِكَ الْمُتَّهَمِينَ كَانُوا مَعْرُوفِينَ بِالشَّرِّ وَظَهَرَتْ الرِّيبَةُ عَلَيْهِمْ. وَهَكَذَا حَكَمَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِالْقَسَامَةِ فِي الدِّمَاءِ إذَا كَانَ هُنَاكَ لَوْثٌ يَغْلِبُ عَلَى الظَّنِّ صِدْقُ الْمُدَّعِينَ؛ فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الْأُمُورَ مِنْ الْحُدُودِ فِي الْمَصَالِحِ الْعَامَّةِ؛ لَيْسَتْ مِنْ الْحُقُوقِ الْخَاصَّةِ فَلَوْلَا الْقَسَامَةُ فِي الدِّمَاءِ لَأَفْضَى إلَى سَفْكِ الدِّمَاءِ فَيَقْتُلُ الرَّجُلُ عَدُوَّهُ خُفْيَةً وَلَا يُمْكِنُ أَوْلِيَاءَ الْمَقْتُولِ إقَامَةُ الْبَيِّنَةِ؛ وَالْيَمِينُ عَلَى الْقَاتِلِ وَالسَّارِقِ وَالْقَاطِعِ سَهْلَةٌ فَإِنَّ مَنْ يَسْتَحِلُّ هَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ لَا يَكْتَرِثُ بِالْيَمِينِ. وَقَوْلُ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ 
{لَوْ يُعْطَى النَّاسُ بِدَعْوَاهُمْ لَادَّعَى قَوْمٌ دِمَاءَ قَوْمٍ وَأَمْوَالَهُمْ؛ وَلَكِنَّ الْيَمِينَ عَلَى الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ}
 هَذَا فِيمَا لَا يُمْكِنُ مِنْ الْمُدَّعِي حُجَّةٌ غَيْرَ الدَّعْوَى فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُعْطَى بِهَا شَيْئًا وَلَكِنْ يَحْلِفُ الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ.
 فَأَمَّا إذَا أَقَامَ شَاهِدًا بِالْمَالِ فَإِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدْ حَكَمَ فِي الْمَالِ بِشَاهِدِ وَيَمِينٍ وَهُوَ قَوْلُ فُقَهَاءِ الْحِجَازِ وَأَهْلِ الْحَدِيثِ كَمَالِكِ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِمْ وَإِذَا كَانَ فِي دَعْوَى الدَّمِ لَوْثٌ فَقَدْ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِلْمُدَّعِينَ:
 
{أَتَحْلِفُونَ خَمْسِينَ يَمِينًا وَتَسْتَحِقُّونَ دَمَ صَاحِبِكُمْ؟}
translated_text:
food and two coats of mail belonging to some of the Ansār. The owner of the property came to complain to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Some people then came forward and falsely vouched for the accused. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, believed those who vouched for them and reproached the owner of the property. Allah then revealed this verse.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not tell the owner of the property, “Produce evidence,” nor did he have the accused swear oaths, because those accused were known for wrongdoing and there were evident grounds for suspecting them.

Likewise, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ruled by qasāma—the procedure of sworn oaths in homicide cases—when there were supporting indications making the claimants’ truthfulness probable. These matters concern penal sanctions serving the public interest, not private rights. Without qasāma in homicide cases, bloodshed would ensue: a man could kill his enemy in secret, while the victim’s next of kin would be unable to produce evidence. Swearing an oath is easy for a murderer, thief, or highway robber, for someone who regards such deeds as permissible will think little of an oath.

As for the Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Were people granted their claims merely on their allegations, some would claim the lives and property of others. Rather, the oath rests upon the defendant.”

This applies where the claimant can offer no proof beyond the allegation itself. Nothing is awarded on that basis; instead, the defendant swears an oath.

If, however, the claimant produces one witness concerning property, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ruled in property cases on the basis of one witness and an oath. This is the position of the jurists of the Hijāz and the scholars of hadith, such as Mālik, al-Shāfi‘ī, Ahmad, and others. When there were supporting indications in a homicide claim, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to the claimants:

“Will you swear fifty oaths and thereby establish your claim concerning your companion’s blood?”

translated_text:
The same applies to “highway robbers” and “thieves.” This concerns the public interest, not private rights. People cannot be secure in their lives and property, in their homes or on the roads, unless such offenders are deterred by amputation. Requiring each of them to swear an oath does not deter them.

For this reason, the jurists agree that a highway robber acting to seize property must be executed, and that his execution is a prescribed punishment owed to Allah, not a matter left to the discretion of the slain person’s next of kin. They explain that he did not kill the victim because of any personal grievance against him; rather, he killed him for his property. To him, there is no difference between this victim and anyone else. Executing him therefore serves the public interest, and the ruler must enforce it.

Likewise, a “thief” does not seek one particular person’s property; rather, he seeks to take this person’s property and that person’s property. Thus, amputating his hand is a binding right owed to Allah, not to the property owner. The owner recovers his property, and the thief’s hand is amputated. Even if the owner says, “I give him my property,” the punishment of amputation is not waived. Thus, Safwān said to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“I give him my cloak.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, replied:

“Why did you not do that before bringing him?”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, also said:

“Whoever intercedes to prevent one of Allah’s prescribed punishments has opposed Allah in His command. Whoever knowingly argues a false case remains under Allah’s displeasure until he desists. Whoever says something about a Muslim that is not true of him will be confined in Radghat al-Khabāl—the mire of filth—until he frees himself from what he has said.”

He also said to al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwām:

“Once cases involving prescribed punishments reach the ruler, may Allah curse the intercessor and the one whose intercession is accepted.”

translated_text:
A similar case is that of someone shown to possess property which he is obliged to produce: for example, a debtor who is found to have concealed his wealth and insists on remaining imprisoned, or someone who holds property in trust but fails to return it to its rightful owner, and whose dishonesty has become evident. Such a person is not asked to swear an oath; rather, he is beaten until he produces the property he is obliged to produce or discloses its whereabouts. This is illustrated by the following account:

In the year of Khaybar, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke to al-Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwām concerning the paternal uncle of Huyayy ibn Akhtab. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had concluded a peace agreement with them stipulating that the gold and silver would belong to him. He asked this man:

“Where is Huyayy ibn Akhtab’s treasure?”

He replied:

“O Muhammad, expenses and wars have consumed it.”

He said:

“There was a great deal of wealth, and too little time has elapsed for that.”

Then he said to al-Zubayr:

“Take charge of this man.”

Al-Zubayr subjected him to some torture, whereupon he directed them to the treasure in a ruined building nearby.

When this man said, “Expenses and wars have consumed it,” ordinary experience contradicted his claim, so no heed was paid to it. Rather, the Prophet ordered that he be punished until he directed them to the property. The same ruling therefore applies to anyone who takes other people’s property and claims that it has been lost in circumstances where ordinary experience contradicts his claim.

He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was also asked:

A man had gold sewn into his garment and, forgetting about it, gave the garment to a washerman. When the washerman returned it after washing it, he found that the place where the gold had been sewn in had been unstitched, and the gold was missing. What is the ruling concerning this?

Answer:

Either the defendant swears an oath clearing himself of liability, or the claimant swears that the defendant took the gold unlawfully, in which case the defendant must compensate him for it. If the washerman is known for wicked conduct, and the opened seam gives evident grounds for suspicion, it is permissible to beat him and subject him to discretionary punishment. Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ - قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ -:
عَنْ أَقْوَامٍ يَقْطَعُونَ الطَّرِيقَ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَيَقْتُلُونَ مَنْ يُمَانَعُهُمْ عَنْ مَالِهِ وَيَفْجُرُونَ بِحَرِيمِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَيُعَذِّبُونَ كُلَّ مَنْ يَمْسِكُونَهُ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى حَتَّى يَدُلَّهُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؛ ثُمَّ الْإِمَامُ بَلَغَهُ خَبَرُهُمْ؛ فَأَمَرَ السُّلْطَانُ بَعْضَ النَّاسِ أَنْ يَرُوحَ إلَيْهِمْ وَيَمْنَعَهُمْ مِنْ قَتْلِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَأَخْذِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ؛ فَخَرَجُوا عَلَيْهِ وَقَالُوا الْمُسَيَّرِينَ إلَيْهِمْ؛ وَامْتَنَعُوا مِنْ طَاعَةِ السُّلْطَانِ فَهَلْ يَحِلُّ قِتَالُهُمْ أَمْ لَا؟ وَهَلْ إذَا أَخَذَ السُّلْطَانُ مِنْ مَالِهِمْ شَيْئًا وَبَاعَهُ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ يَحِلُّ لِأَحَدِ أَنْ يَشْتَرِيَهُ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، نَعَمْ يَحِلُّ قِتَالُ هَؤُلَاءِ بَلْ يَجِبُ؛ وَإِذَا أَخَذَ السُّلْطَانُ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ بِإِزَاءِ مَا أَخَذُوهُ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَلَمْ يَعْرِفْ مُسْتَحِقَّهُ جَازَ الشِّرَاءُ مِنْهُ وَإِنْ كَانُوا أَخَذُوا شَيْئًا مِنْ أَمْوَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَفِي أَخْذِ أَمْوَالِهِمْ خِلَافٌ بَيْنَ الْفُقَهَاءِ. وَإِذَا قَلَّدَ السُّلْطَانُ أَحَدَ الْقَوْلَيْنِ بِطَرِيقَةِ سَاغَ لَهُ ذَلِكَ.
translated_text:
Chapter: The Prescribed Punishment for Highway Robbers

Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah sanctify his soul—was asked:

Some people waylay Muslims, kill anyone who resists their attempts to take his property, violate Muslim women, and torture every Muslim they capture, male or female, until they disclose the whereabouts of some Muslim property. News of them reached the imam, and the ruler ordered some men to go and prevent them from killing Muslims and taking their property. They then rose against him, addressed those dispatched against them, and refused to obey the ruler. Is it lawful to fight them? If the ruler seizes some of their property and sells it to Muslims, is anyone permitted to buy it?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. Yes, fighting these people is lawful; indeed, it is obligatory. If the ruler takes from their property an amount corresponding to what they took from the Muslims’ property, and does not know who is entitled to it, it is permissible to purchase it from him. If they have taken some of the Muslims’ property, the jurists differ concerning the seizure of their property. If the ruler follows either of the two opinions as his course of action, he is permitted to do so.

وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
عَنْ الْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ؛
 الَّذِينَ يَسْتَحِلُّونَ أَمْوَالَ النَّاسِ وَدِمَاءَهُمْ:
 مِثْلَ السَّارِقِ وَقَاطِعِ الطَّرِيقِ: هَلْ لِلْإِنْسَانِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُمْ شَيْئًا مِنْ مَالِهِ؟ أَوْ يُقَاتِلَهُمْ؟
 وَهَلْ إذَا قَتَلَ رَجُلٌ أُحُدًا مِنْهُمْ:
 فَهَلْ يَكُونُ مِمَّنْ يُنْسَبُ إلَى النِّفَاقِ؟ وَهَلْ عَلَيْهِ إثْمٌ فِي قَتْلِ مَنْ طَلَبَ قَتْلَهُ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
أَجَمَعَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى جَوَازِ مُقَاتَلَةِ قُطَّاعِ الطَّرِيقِ وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{مَنْ قُتِلَ دُونَ مَالِهِ فَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ}
 . 
" فَالْقُطَّاعُ "
 إذَا طَلَبُوا مَالَ الْمَعْصُومِ لَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُمْ شَيْئًا بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ؛ بَلْ يَدْفَعُهُمْ بِالْأَسْهَلِ فَالْأَسْهَلِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْدَفِعُوا إلَّا بِالْقِتَالِ فَلَهُ أَنْ يُقَاتِلَهُمْ فَإِنْ قُتِلَ كَانَ شَهِيدًا وَإِنْ قَتَلَ وَاحِدًا مِنْهُمْ عَلَى هَذَا الْوَجْهِ كَانَ دَمُهُ هَدَرًا؛ وَكَذَلِكَ إذَا طَلَبُوا دَمَهُ كَانَ لَهُ أَنْ يَدْفَعَهُمْ وَلَوْ بِالْقَتْلِ إجْمَاعًا؛ لَكِنَّ الدَّفْعَ عَنْ الْمَالِ لَا يَجِبُ بَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يُعْطِيَهُمْ الْمَالَ وَلَا يُقَاتِلَهُمْ. وَأَمَّا الدَّفْعُ عَنْ النَّفْسِ فَفِي وُجُوبِهِ قَوْلَانِ هُمَا رِوَايَتَانِ عَنْ أَحْمَد.
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

Concerning those who spread corruption in the land and treat people’s property and lives as lawful to take, such as thieves and highway robbers: may a person give them some of his property, or may he fight them? If a man kills one of them, is he to be accused of hypocrisy? Does he incur any sin by killing someone who sought to kill him?

He answered:

The Muslims unanimously agree that fighting highway robbers is permissible. It is authentically established that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr.”

If “highway robbers” demand the property of someone entitled to legal protection, he is not obliged to give them anything, by agreement of the imams. Rather, he should repel them using the least force necessary, escalating only as needed. If they cannot be repelled except by fighting, he may fight them. If he is killed, he is a martyr; if he kills one of them in these circumstances, no liability is incurred for that person’s death. Likewise, if they seek to kill him, he may repel them, even by killing them, according to unanimous agreement.

However, defending one’s property is not obligatory: a person may give them the property rather than fight them. As for defending one’s life, there are two opinions concerning whether it is obligatory, corresponding to two positions reported from Ahmad.

وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
عَنْ تَاجِرٍ نَصَبَ عَلَيْهِ جَمَاعَةٌ؛ وَأَخَذُوا مَبْلَغًا فَحَمَلَهُمْ لِوَلِيِّ الْأَمْرِ؛ وَعَاقَبَهُمْ حَتَّى أَقَرُّوا بِالْمَالِ وَهُمْ مَحْبُوسُونَ عَلَى الْمَالِ وَلَمْ يُعْطُوهُ شَيْئًا وَهُمْ مُصِرُّونَ عَلَى أَنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْطُونَهُ شَيْئًا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، هَؤُلَاءِ مَنْ كَانَ الْمَالُ بِيَدِهِ وَامْتَنَعَ مِنْ إعْطَائِهِ فَإِنَّهُ يُضْرَبُ حَتَّى يُؤَدِّيَ الْمَالَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ لِغَيْرِهِ. وَمَنْ كَانَ قَدْ غَيَّبَ الْمَالَ وَجَحَدَ مَوْضِعَهُ فَإِنَّهُ يُضْرَبُ حَتَّى يَدُلَّ عَلَى مَوْضِعِهِ. وَمَنْ كَانَ مُتَّهَمًا لَا يَعْرِفُ هَلْ مَعَهُ مِنْ الْمَالِ شَيْءٌ أَمْ لَا؛ فَإِنَّهُ يَجُوزُ ضَرْبُهُ مُعَاقَبَةً لَهُ عَلَى مَا فَعَلَ مِنْ الْكَذِبِ وَالظُّلْمِ. وَيُقَرَّرُ مَعَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمَالِ أَيْنَ هُوَ. وَيُطْلَبُ مِنْهُ إحْضَارُهُ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

Concerning a merchant whom a group of people defrauded, taking a sum of money from him. He brought them before the ruler, who punished them until they confessed to taking the money. They remain imprisoned over the money, but have given him nothing and insist that they will give him nothing.

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. Whoever among them has the money in his possession and refuses to hand it over is to be beaten until he hands over the money belonging to someone else that he holds. Whoever has concealed the money and denies knowing its whereabouts is to be beaten until he reveals its location.

As for anyone suspected of holding the money, when it is not known whether he has any of it, he may be beaten as punishment for the lying and wrongdoing he has committed. He is also to be pressed to disclose where the money is and required to produce it. And Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ - قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ وَنَوَّرَ ضَرِيحَهُ -:
عَنْ ثَلَاثَةٍ مِنْ اللُّصُوصِ أَخَذَ اثْنَانِ مِنْهُمْ جِمَالًا وَالثَّالِثُ قَتَلَ الْجِمَالَ:
 هَلْ تُقْتَلُ الثَّلَاثَةُ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا كَانَ الثَّلَاثَةُ حَرَامِيَّةً اجْتَمَعُوا لِيَأْخُذُوا الْمَالَ بِالْمُحَارَبَةِ قُتِلَ الثَّلَاثَةُ وَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي بَاشَرَ الْقَتْلَ وَاحِدًا مِنْهُمْ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked—may Allah sanctify his soul and illuminate his grave:

Concerning three thieves: two of them took some camels, and the third killed the camels. Are all three to be put to death?

He answered:

If the three were bandits who had joined together to seize property by armed force, all three are to be put to death, even if only one of them actually carried out the killing. And Allah knows best.
